Gap on BASE_SHA 55d80326 (VERIFIED by reading + by the failing base runs): no database object models offline authorization. The shared contract packages/shared-types/src/offlineAuthorization.ts (OFFLINE_PRO_LEASE_MAX_SECONDS = 7*24*60*60, OFFLINE_FREE_ALLOCATION_POLICY: identity-lifetime budget, allocation ≠ consumption, never auto-released) has no backing table/RPC; `grep -rn offline supabase/migrations` on base returns nothing. public.reserve_analysis_permit() (supabase/migrations/20260902150000_free_rating_identity_ledger.sql, the `v_count := public.lifetime_scored_count() + reserved` branch) and public.access_state() (same file) only count lifetime_scored_count() + live analysis_permits, so a disconnected device's outstanding allocation could never be represented, let alone conserved. supabase/tests/security_regression.sql K24/K27 allowlists (RLS-table and RPC inventories) had no offline entries and db_migrations_rls_indexes.test.ts pinned nothing about device/grant/ledger objects.

Fix (commits 94ab540c tests, 2c8fd4f5 test syntax/format follow-up, 66a70a5e implementation): forward migration supabase/migrations/20260908120000_offline_device_grants.sql adds public.offline_devices (owner + installation_key_id, attestation_environment/state, unique per (user_id, installation_key_id)), public.offline_grants (per device, monotonic generation, entitlement_source free|verified_store, CHECK expires_at <= issued_at + interval '7 days', CHECK entitlement_expires_at is null or expires_at <= entitlement_expires_at, immutable via guard_offline_grant trigger), and public.offline_allocation_ledger (append-only for every role via guard_offline_ledger_append_only; no FKs so rows outlive device/account deletion; events allocated|consumed|released with guard_offline_ledger_event enforcing one terminal event per ticket, owner-matched scored shot on consume, no double charge for shots already backed by an online permit; identity_hashes stored on each row). All three tables: RLS enabled, restrictive api_requests_only policy, all anon/authenticated/PUBLIC grants revoked, owner + ordering indexes. New RPCs register_offline_device / issue_offline_grant / consume_offline_ticket / release_offline_ticket are pinned (search_path='') SECURITY DEFINER guarded by api_private.is_active_session() and scoped to auth.uid(); issue_offline_grant takes pg_advisory_xact_lock(access_lock_key(uid)) and allocates free tickets only while lifetime_scored_count() + live reservations + offline_hold_count() < 2, issues a verified_store lease only for an EFFECTIVE entitlement (premium and expires_at null or > now()) bounded by least(now()+7d, entitlement expires_at); stale premium rows take the free path. access_state() and reserve_analysis_permit() are redefined (grants preserved) to add offline_hold_count() so allocated + consumed(=scored) + reserved ≤ 2 per identity lifetime. No cron/sweep/cascade releases an allocation: grant expiry, device or account deletion, key replacement and the existing permit sweep leave the ledger untouched; release is only ever an explicit terminal event and is not a re-credit.

non_blocking_issues: Implementer claim 'TRUNCATE rejected' for the ledger is not what the migration does: the append-only trigger is BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE only; TRUNCATE is not row-triggered and service_role holds TRUNCATE via hosted default privileges (verified: has_table_privilege('service_role','public.offline_allocation_ledger','TRUNCATE') = t; authenticated = f). Consistent with the repo's other append-only ledgers (no existing migration has a TRUNCATE trigger), so not a regression, but the claim should not be repeated. A later forward migration could add a BEFORE TRUNCATE trigger.

The four mutating RPCs (+offline_hold_count) are SECURITY DEFINER granted to authenticated. Each is gated by is_active_session()/is_api_request(), auth.uid()-scoped, search_path='' pinned and matrix-tested (T8), so no leak was found, but they are a departure from the 'user RPCs stay SECURITY INVOKER' K28 convention; K28's enumerated list was left unchanged (not weakened) and the static pin asserts the definer guard. Acceptable for this package; note for the edge-index follow-up.

consume_offline_ticket()/release_offline_ticket() match the allocation by a.user_id = auth.uid() only, while offline_hold_count() also matches by identity hash. After delete-and-recreate (T6) the identity inherits the hold but the new account can neither consume nor release that ticket, so it stays outstanding for the identity's lifetime (conservative: never over-grants, never auto-reclaims). Intended per invariant, but support has no RPC-level path to release it; a later package may want an explicit owner-recovery path.

issue_offline_grant() has no idempotency key: every call mints a new grant generation (outstanding tickets are re-issued, never duplicated, so conservation holds). Edge wiring should dedupe retries or accept generation churn.

Follow-up wiring risk (outside this package's write_paths): an offline scored shot must be inserted (analysis_permit_id null) and its ticket consumed in one transaction by the Edge Function; a crash between the two leaves scored+1 and hold+1 for the identity (conservative, but permanently burns one free rating). Not reachable today: no Edge route calls the new RPCs, so production hold counts are 0 until the edge-index package lands.

Commit 22cacfd5 (tests first): W04 sections of security_regression.sql incl. the new T10 delete-and-recreate recovery scenario and T4/T8 hardening, plus the static W04-01 pin. Commit cf659b55: test-only pg_temp definer helpers so the client/service role reads the ledger without widening production grants, Prettier re-format. Commit 1da63a1e: the forward migration 20260908120000_offline_device_grants.sql reusing the sound r1 design (offline_devices, offline_grants with table-level 7-day/entitlement-expiry bounds, append-only no-FK offline_allocation_ledger, five API-gated RPCs, offline_hold_count() folded into access_state()/reserve_analysis_permit() under access_lock_key(uid)) and fixing the r1 break at its root: ledger rows carry installation_key_id (NOT NULL, bounded) and identity_hashes; ownership for re-issue/consume/release is api_private.offline_ticket_owned_by(owner uid, identity hashes, caller) = same account OR overlapping sign-in identity (api_private.offline_identity_hashes(uid) via free_rating_identity_hash over auth.identities); issue_offline_grant() re-issues outstanding tickets matched by the device's installation key rather than by device row id (which cascades away on deletion); guard_offline_ledger_event() replaces the UUID-only owner check with the predicate and pins terminal events to the allocation's installation key; release_offline_ticket() accepts only unused_ticket_returned (support_review is a table-level audit reason); every offline table/sequence privilege is revoked from service_role so the append-only triggers cannot be bypassed by TRUNCATE.
regression_tests_added: supabase/tests/security_regression.sql (W04 sections T1-T10; T4 client cannot self-assert support_review; T8 service_role holds no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE/REFERENCES/TRIGGER on the three offline tables and TRUNCATE is refused; T10 account deletion + re-creation with the same Apple identity: hold follows the identity, a different installation never inherits the old ticket, a different identity cannot consume/release it, the original installation key re-issues exactly the outstanding ticket without allocating a second one, consume is exactly-once and idempotent, a second ticket cannot consume the same shot, support closes the remaining ticket through the table and it still counts against the entitlement)

supabase/functions/api/__wf__/db_migrations_rls_indexes.test.ts (static pin 'W04-01: device registry, per-device offline grants...': migration in chain, api_private.offline_identity_hashes + offline_ticket_owned_by definers with empty search_path and no client/service grants, ledger installation_key_id NOT NULL + bounded, issue/consume/release lookups identity-aware and keyed by installation key, event guard uses the ownership predicate and pins the installation key, client release limited to unused_ticket_returned, all offline table privileges revoked from service_role)
residual_risks: Identity-aware recovery follows the free-rating identity model: a re-created account with a DIFFERENT provider subject (e.g. Apple then Google) is a different identity and cannot recover the old installation's ticket; only explicit support review (privileged table write in the identity's name on the same installation key) can close it — consistent with OFFLINE_FREE_ALLOCATION_POLICY.recovery.
